name: Nige
title: RT by @nigescore: Astra Ultra did not cook sports-grade vision AI. Gave it a 30s football clip from our subnet private track. Frame-level events, JSON, annotated video. Ground truth and the published scoring rules only after it committed. 22 predictions. 17 real events. 15 inside the action windows. 7 extras. 2 misses. Precision 68.18%. Recall 88.24%. F1 76.92%. Our Bittensor eval, SN44: 0%. Matches after timing decay: 16.538 False positives: −20.300 GT weight: 25.600 score = max(0, (16.538 − 20.300) / 25.600) = 0 Three extra take-ons and two extra tackles were 14.6 penalty points. It also misread the late interception/clearance. Rare actions pay more when you hit them and tax you harder when you invent them. Perfect timestamps on the matches still would not have cleared that bill. This was one offline replay of the published scorer. Unchanged preds. Not live latency. Not a season. The point is simpler than the arithmetic. F1 is what you post. SN44 is what you get paid on. Real matches, messy cameras, hard negatives, and a 30-second clock are not the same sport as a nice 15s clip to aura farm on Twitter.

name: Covenant AI
title: RT by @covenant_ai: PULSE (also called Delta weight sync) has become one of the most important ideas in RL infrastructure this year. Our paper, posted on February 3, explained why it loses nothing. At RL learning rates, about 99% of each step's weight updates disappear in the BF16 cast, so the inference workers never see them. Since then, @huggingface has built Delta Weight Sync for TRL and vLLM on that argument. @FireworksAI_HQ cites PULSE, and its ARCv3 compressor now makes the updates even smaller. This week @humansand reported pausing inference for only about 220 milliseconds per update on Blackwell GPUs. PULSE has now been accepted at AXIOM, a @NeurIPSConf 2026 workshop. https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03839

title: "We're not afraid of hyper-intelligent bot swarms on the internet. We use them to optimise our technology." When we launched RedTeam almost two years ago we could clearly see where the internet was heading. We've since seen clients with over 90% of their traffic made up of not just automation but highly intelligent bot swarms, capable of bypassing any traditional detection mechanism. The only way to combat a threat like this is to welcome it and learn from it. By constantly ingesting and evolving attack vectors from a hive mind of miners, a Bittensor powered defence has now become the only reliable source of protection on the internet.

name: Jon Durbin
title: Here's a very crude simplified chutes roadmap/plan, for near term: - move the most unprofitable things off of the subnet, including today's announcement of some (not all) additional inference options (not paid via emissions) - this allows us to scale the things we want and need to avoid capacity issues/better direct incentive - this includes models we use to build data pipelines and relationships to other teams/networks/etc - add options that are completely revenue positive (hourly pricing/rentals/simple docker based jobs/etc), TEE, private, secure, priced above cost, more extensive version of private chutes we have today basically - expand the hourly compute offerings to also include CPU only (e.g. to run agents, web browsers, sandboxes, non-GPU work of any kind) - use some of the incentive for ideally non-datacenter based model training and serving - build a non-extractable product on chutes from the models we build, via dynamic edge nodes, possibly from the epigenesis work (smaller faster cheaper faster than lora customizations from the sparse sections of pretrained model, participant supplied) - models and pipeline etc. will be open source, the customization and ensemble thereof will live only in chutes, inc. the continuously evolving set of served variations/RL/etc. We'd like, to the extent we can, attract participants who want to build and have no obligation to pay datacenters or any particular hardware vendor, to keep the value inside the subnet at all times by attacking sell pressure at the source (DC commitments, chip purchases, etc). We will continue to have secure TEE inference and GPUs; not elimating anything wholesale, just focusing more on a commodity that doesn't have to flow out to DCs and single hardware vendors. NVIDIA reportedly has 75% profit margins, revenue for the sake of revenue fueling GPU reselling goes straight to one place, basically. Fine, I guess, but I'd rather work together as individuals with whatever hardware we can bring, to a reasonable degree.
